overall_summary: Space anomalies, specifically extreme planetary environments and cosmic oddities, are the clear growth drivers for FACTVERSE, capturing the highest views and engagement. Conversely, cognitive psychology and brain-related facts are severely underperforming, struggling to capture initial viewer interest.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,018 views), 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) represent the channel's peak performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space conditions, focusing on highly visual, hostile exoplanets and cosmic phenomena using 21-second formats.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Visited the Sunscreen Planet?' achieved 346 views, outperforming standard factual trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Frame cosmic facts as hypothetical survival scenarios to increase viewer retention and emotional investment.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple uploads) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from abstract internal psychology topics and redirect production resources toward external, highly visual cosmic mysteries.
